title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s White Day Part 1
text: It’s been half a month since that rotten Valentine’s Day. We’d been scrambling to make up for the damage we caused on Valentine’s Day. By the way, the Doll Festival went off without a hitch, thanks to Imiya, the Rumo clan, and a bunch of folks with nimble fingers who handled things for me.

The damage I’m talking about is the Chocolate Monster incident. Seriously… Back when the Chocolate Monster caused trouble—not to mention the Gaelion incident—I fled to Zeltoble via a portal. At first, I thought I’d gotten away with it, but the Chocolate Monster came after me using a weapon it had absorbed from Fohl. Because I kept running from there, the damage… well, it snowballed out of control.

If I’d been caught, the Chocolate Monster—which was acting to fulfill Gaelion’s wish—would’ve done something truly unspeakable to me. The cost was high, but I… was able to protect myself, and that’s what saved me. As a result, I ended up having to pay compensation, so I’m using Filo and Keel to plan a White Day event.
“Hey, Naofumi? This is supposed to be a ‘return-the-favor’ event, so are you really going to make the fans buy white chocolate and merchandise?”
“Yeah, fans like this will buy limited-edition items and stuff—even though they’re the ones who are supposed to be giving the gifts in the first place.”

The White Day event is supposed to be where people who bought “Filo’s Handmade Chocolates” send their own gifts to Filo in return… but we’re narrowing the scope even further. We’re steering it so that fans purchase their gifts for Filo from Filo-related shops and have them delivered to her.

If it goes well, we can reuse the items we receive. Since we might be swamped with inventory, we’ll use our connections with a jewelry merchant who also runs a sweets business to sell them off at a low price after the event. Depending on the exchange rate, we should turn a nice profit without even covering our costs.

“Ah, this time we don’t need to go to all that trouble. Just pour the mixture into a standard mold and stamp it—that’s enough. Just make sure to wrap them up, though. We’re recycling them, after all.”

Thanks to our experience making chocolates last time, we’ve built up some know-how. As a result, the work is going more smoothly than last time. At this rate, we should have no trouble making it to the big day.
“Naofumi’s still just as crafty as ever, isn’t he…”
Melty murmurs as she watches him working on the White Day items.
“What can I say? The damages were huge, after all.”
I picked a bad place to run to. If they chase me, I’ll just take them down along with Raphtalia and Filo. Thinking so optimistically and flying to Zeltoble was my downfall.
“Naofumi, you should think things through before you run away.”
“Well, yeah. But if I’d fled anywhere else, I’d probably be suffering from morning sickness and throwing up by next month or so.”
“Ugh… I guess you’re right. I don’t want to see Naofumi’s belly gradually getting bigger.”
“Seriously, stop it… with that kind of talk.”

Just the thought of getting pregnant by the Dragon Emperor would be a nightmare. It’s way too graphic. Seriously… that little Gaelion. Well, he’s got his own internal struggles to some extent, and at the last minute, he tried to escape just like he did with the Lars Dragon.

Even so, I decided to put him on probation—or rather, keep him away. He’s keeping a low profile now, but Taniko comes by to report on him from time to time. Apparently, he’s picked up a new hobby—just like Atla—of collecting the stuff I’ve thrown away. His mom, Gaelion, was complaining that as soon as he found out I was going to take a bath, he chased after me, and once he saw me get out, he started drinking the bathwater.
It’s absolutely disgusting. The fact that I actually think Filo is better than him shows just how messed up I am… Anyway, I’ll just focus on my work and try to keep my sanity.
“Next up is Keel’s merchandise. Imiya, what’s the status?”
“I’ve just confirmed that we’ve reached the 3,000th Keel-kun plushie. Are we making any more?”
“We’ll sell them at a slightly higher unit price, so that’s enough. Move on to the next task… After all, we’re putting that crepe-loving dog in a musical.”

While we were discussing the next event, Filo threw a tantrum, insisting she wanted to be part of it. Since Filo seemed to find theater really interesting, a musical was the best way to incorporate her into the show. That’s why Filo’s schedule is now absolutely packed. As for Keel, he has a “physical contact session” scheduled—not a handshake event. He’s more of a popular mascot than a full-fledged idol.
“Yes. Understood.”
Imiya always obeys without a single complaint in situations like this. Even though the work itself is tough.
“Sorry to put you through this again.”
I gently ruffled her hair from behind.
“Ah… I’ll do my best.”

Imiya hurried off at a brisk pace to join Keel. Well, Keel seems to be enjoying himself to some extent, so I’m sure it’ll be fine. I’m not exactly free of guilt, though—especially since I’m trying to make Filo and Keel pay off my debt… or rather, compensate for the damages I caused.

I’ve already paid off most of the debt with my own pocket money, but I get anxious when my funds run low. After all, I hold the title of Grand Duke of Melromarc, a major power. The amount of money and land I own is probably among the highest in this world.

If the wealth rankings from the real world existed here, I’d rank quite high. So, to be honest, I’m actually quite financially secure. Well, it’s just that old habits from when I was strapped for cash have resurfaced, and since the outlook for raising funds for the next reconstruction effort has become uncertain, I’ve ended up being a bit greedy.
“Ah, and then—…”
“Naofumi-sama?”
Raphtalia calls out to me. Well, the next problem… is my own personal business, so I guess it’s fine.
“So? Did you need something?”
“Oh, yes. A letter has arrived from the chocolate farmer. And… one from Kage-san, too.”
Ah, the regular reports for me. I take the letters and documents and read them. …I found myself instinctively putting my hand to my forehead.
“What’s wrong?”
“Ugh… there’s a report on what’s become of that jerk of an old man.”
“W-what happened?”

That’s the jerk of an old man I ran into when I went to buy Valentine’s Day chocolate. I think “the Robin Hood-type old man” pretty much sums him up. A commotion broke out because of the chocolate monster boss he captured, and the whole incident wrapped up thanks to the crappy chocolate he made. Technically, he’s a behind-the-scenes hero, but I’m not giving him any credit.

More importantly, it’s the contents of the letter. He held a grudge against me, escaped from the holding cell, and had been on the run toward my territory… that’s right. But apparently, after witnessing the unusual plants and new species of monsters in my village, he must have painfully realized just how far behind he was—and was captured in a dazed state near my territory. I hear he’s back home now and has become remarkably well-behaved.

I don’t even know where to start with this… The security was so lax he managed to escape, but it’s impressive he had the determination to make it all the way to my place. And then, seeing my plants and monsters, he was left speechless, huh? Though he is behaving himself, the letter complains that whenever something comes up, he starts chanting the word “talent” over and over, which is annoying.

You know the type… the kind of person who, when someone else succeeds, belittles themselves by saying it’s all down to “talent” and that they’re different. They brush off all of that person’s hard work as just talent. Every time they open their mouth, they start saying things like, “That guy’s a genius.” People like that end up this way because they can’t understand what a genius has built up over time. Well, not that I’m a genius myself, mind you.

I hate to say it, but I’m just an ordinary person. It’s not just this shield—anyone who possesses Legendary Weapons gains various abilities regardless of their own skill level. How they use it is up to them, but at least I’m not confident I’ve fully mastered the shield’s power. If this were my other self, maybe to some extent… well, never mind that.

Either way, that damn old man—he definitely hasn’t given up. If he manages to create something to counter me, this will flare up again. I’ll need to keep an eye on him, and if he tries anything, I’ll warn the organizations in the area to crush his spirit before he even gets started.
The Robin Hood-type guy also sent me a thank-you letter. I’d decided to give him a slightly bigger cut, so I hope he’ll keep doing a good job…
“So, that’s a problem already taken care of.”
“Well… how should I put this? I’ve actually received another letter.”
“Hm?”
A letter from the next day? It’s from the Robin Hood-type guy’s sister.
“I sent one yesterday as well, but I’ve discovered that my father is secretly building a new contraption. He’s hiding it very cleverly, so I’m still investigating. I’m enclosing a rough sketch.”
There was… a drawing of what looked like a little boy peeing. Without hesitation, I wrote a letter with instructions at a nearby desk and sent a messenger off in the shadows.
It’s obvious at a glance. It’d be fine if this were just art, but knowing that damn old man… It’s a given he’ll mix in chocolate to make something awful.

I’ll let him run wild for now, but once his invention takes shape, I’ll use him as a test subject myself. Most likely… he’ll try to make white chocolate come out of wherever it’s supposed to. There are plenty of “fountain” gags out there, after all.

Anyway, with no particular problems like the ones we had on Valentine’s Day, White Day finally arrived. I woke up early and got to work making desserts in the village kitchen. After all, I’d received chocolate from just about everyone in the village. A snack should be plenty as a White Day return gift, right?
Donuts, marshmallows, candy, and white chocolate. There are a lot of heavy items first thing in the morning, but I plan to set these up in a separate corner so people can help themselves.
“Good morning, big bro—there’s a ton of snacks!”
Keel is staring intently at the snack corner while wagging his tail.
“These are for everyone, so don’t eat too many.”
“Okay! These are all for Big Bro’s White Day gifts!”

But… even though I’m supposed to be giving these to the girls, why does it feel like I’m giving presents to kids? Well, these guys may look big on the outside, but inside, a lot of them are still kids. Come to think of it, they actually were kids.
“Good morning, Naofumi-sama.”
“Rafu.”
“Good morning, Raphtalia, Raph-chan.”

I gave Raphtalia and Raph-chan each a Bûche de Noël made of white chocolate as a White Day gift. I could’ve gone with a “Raph-chan Cake” or something, but I played it safe. You see, Raphtalia isn’t really into anything too outlandish; she prefers things with a sophisticated touch like this. For better or worse, she’s very much a girl.
A “Raph-chan” cake might look good, but it’d be a disaster once you cut into it… And Raph-chan would be the one eating it, right? It’d feel like cannibalism, and I’d probably regret it. Better not.
“Wow… thank you so much.”
“Raph!”
Both Raphtalia and Raph-chan accepted them with happy smiles.
“Lucky you—just you two, Raphtalia-chan and Raph-chan.”
“Keel, yours are over there, aren’t they?”
“Raphtalia and the others’ look better.”
“The grass is always greener on the other side. Give it up.”

It’s that old saying—other people’s stuff always looks better. Plus, you guys prioritize quantity over quality. You eat way more than Raphtalia does. If a small portion were enough, I’d make the same thing for you, but you’d definitely complain that it’s too little.
“Oh my? You guys seem to be having fun today.”
The orca girl, who’d been quiet on Valentine’s Day, came over.
